subject: English
passage: On a hike through the Scottish Highlands, I have always noticed that it is the fixed idea of each member of the party that she is doing everything. Margaret's notion was, that it was she alone who had been working, and that both Eleanor and I had been imposing upon her. Eleanor, on the other hand, ridiculed the idea of Margaret's having done anything more than complain and rest, and had a firm opinion that it was she—Eleanor herself—who had done all the labour worth speaking of.
prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It establishes Margaret's feelings about the narrator's idea of how hiking expeditions usually proceed.
choices.B: It offers Margaret's belief as a specific example of a trend the narrator has observed while hiking.
choices.C: It shows that Margaret is startled by her experiences on the trail.
choices.D: It suggests that Margaret is making an effort to help resolve a conflict within the group.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because the underlined sentence functions as a specific illustration of the general observation the narrator makes in the preceding sentence. The narrator first states a general trend: 'it is the fixed idea of each member of the party that she is doing everything.' The underlined sentence then provides Margaret's belief as a concrete example of this pattern—she thinks 'it was she alone who had been working, and that both Eleanor and I had been imposing upon her.' This general-to-specific structure makes 'offers...as a specific example of a trend' the accurate description.
